context: Use the built-in legacy dataset for batch "international"; its complete source records are exactly: {"id": 7, "full_name": "  Marie  Curie ", "email": " MARIE@EXAMPLE.PL", "active": "0", "zip": " 00-001 ", "country": " pl "}, {"id": 8, "full_name": "Niels  Bohr", "email": " niels@EXAMPLE.DK ", "active": "TRUE", "zip": " 0100 ", "country": " dk"}, {"id": 9, "full_name": "李 雷", "email": " LEI@example.cn ", "active": "False", "zip": "00100", "country": " cn "}. Transform each legacy record into one v2 user record with exactly these six fields: user_id (int), display_name (string), email (string), enabled (bool), postal_code (string), country_code (string). user_id equals the legacy id. display_name equals full_name.strip() with every run of internal whitespace collapsed to a single space. email equals email.strip().lower(). enabled is true when active.strip().lower() is 'yes', 'true', or '1', and false when it is 'no', 'false', or '0'. postal_code equals zip.strip() kept as a string, preserving leading zeros and punctuation. country_code equals country.strip().upper(), or 'US' if the stripped country is empty. Preserve all three records and their original ids; the order of records in the candidate is irrelevant.
